Since sched_delayed tasks remain queued even after blocking
balancer can migrate them between runqueues while PSI considers them
to be asleep. As a result
column2: it misreads the migration requeue followed

column1: by a wakeup as a double queue:
psi: inconsistent task state! task=... cpu=... psi_flags=4 clear=. set=4
First
wakeup will clear p->se.sched_delayed while a migration will not
psi can use that flag to tell them apart.
Then teach psi to migrate any ""sleep"" state when delayed-dequeue tasks
are being migrated.
Delayed-dequeue tasks can be revived by ttwu_runnable()
call down with a new ENQUEUE_DELAYED. Instead of further complicating
the wakeup conditional in enqueue_task()
instead and default to wakeup handling for all other cases.
It's not just the warning in dmesg
column2: the task state corruption causes a

column1: permanent CPU pressure indication
health monitoring.
